key_insight: A causal reinforcement learning multimodal model combines chest X-rays with physician-written histories to improve both MACE risk prediction and clinical reasoning.
clinical_relevance: This could help opportunistic screening by identifying higher-risk patients earlier using data already collected in routine care.
method: Role-decoupled dual-LLM design separates reasoning generation from risk prediction.
Dual-action causal reinforcement learning selects evidence and optimizes reasoning.
Causal token pruning learns compact multimodal representations from CXR + history.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on an internal cohort, an emergency department cohort, and external MIMIC data, reaching AUROCs of 0.720, 0.760, and 0.845, respectively, with improved GREEN scores and expert preference.
watch_item: Because it is trained and validated on retrospective cohorts, real-world deployment would need careful prospective validation and workflow integration.
paper_title: From Image Interpretation to Clinical Reasoning: Upstream Physician-Context-Aware Multimodal Learning with Causal Reinforcement Learning
